clue.text: Dipping into benefits, wife goes off course

indicators.note: dipping into something means going inside it, so the single letter sits within the longer word

parts.note: to serve someone is to benefit them
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife distracted by state benefit payments loses her way.
explanation.definitionFit: To veer suddenly from a straight path is to leave the intended course.

clue.text: Endless kissing distracted singer

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter
a distracted mind is jumbled, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A vocalist is put off by non-stop kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small finch, and songbirds are crossword singers.

clue.text: Former partner backing shop barred from the country

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the shop's name is read backwards

parts.note: a delicatessen

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse who supports a shop has been banned from the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone banished and barred from their homeland has been sent into exile.

clue.text: Greens say they've lost the power to think

definitions.meaning: first meaning: greens are an example of garden produce, as 'say' signals

definitions.text: they've lost the power to think
definitions.meaning: second meaning: people left in a vegetative state, unable to think

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners are mocked as having lost their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' suggests the political party; here it is leafy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage and kale are plant foods, and a person with no mental function is slangily called a vegetable.

clue.text: Shed ends up housing 50

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is reversed
housing means giving a home to, so the number goes inside

parts.note: tips are ends or points
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A garden shed ends up home to fifty things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun for a hut, but it is the past tense of spill.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilt is a past tense meaning poured out or shed, as in spilt blood.

clue.text: Judge employs grasping American lawyer to find traitors

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to employ a thing is to use it
a District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A judge hires a grabby US lawyer to root out betrayers.
explanation.walkthrough: J is the standard abbreviation for judge and DA a US District Attorney; the lawyer sits inside the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name became a common noun for any betrayer.

clue.text: Spooner's acrimonious prison dance

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words trade their initial sounds

parts.note: acrimonious is bitter and jug is slang for prison; swap the opening B and J sounds

explanation.surface: A bitter dance performed in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the B and J of bitter jug.
explanation.definitionFit: The jitterbug was an energetic swing dance popular in the 1940s.

clue.text: Parliament to finish on time

parts.note: to die is to come to an end
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The legislature must wrap up its business punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, such as the Japanese parliament.

clue.text: Back in South Africa, Christopher spotted Fascist symbol

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the abbreviation for South Africa

indicators.note: back signals turning round, so the name and verb are read backwards

parts.note: to spot is to see
Kit is a short form of Christopher

explanation.surface: On returning to South Africa, a man named Christopher noticed a Nazi emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked cross was the emblem of the Nazi party.

clue.text: Spinner from Manx mill works dementedly

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter
acting dementedly is behaving in a crazed, disordered way, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the word cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spinning machine in a mill on the Isle of Man runs wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' looks geographic, but it signals tail removal, after the tailless Manx cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The caterpillar spins a cocoon of silk thread, so it is a natural spinner.

clue.text: Alternative listening that includes one unexpected finale

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the numeral goes in among the other letters
an alternative version is a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An alternative way of listening brings a surprise ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a nasty surprise at the very end, like a scorpion's barb.

clue.text: See 9
Equations targeted by 21st-century thieves?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in maths, equations true for every value of the variables
second meaning: personal details stolen in modern online fraud

explanation.surface: Modern criminals apparently go after mathematical formulas.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, cryptic meaning: identity theft is the typical modern crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematicians call always-true equations by this name, and fraudsters steal people's personal ones.

clue.text: Put away in a clockwise direction

wordplay.note: south to west, which is turning clockwise round the compass

explanation.surface: Tidying things away by turning them clockwise.
explanation.walkthrough: On a compass going from S to W follows the clock hands, so the direction reads as S, TO, W.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow luggage is to pack it away in storage.

clue.text: Note penned by resolute opponent

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so the note is enclosed

parts.note: constant means steadfast
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A determined rival writes a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a contest is an opponent to the others taking part.

clue.text: Medicine cabinet placed on punt by sailor

indicators.note: placing one thing on another sets them side by side in sequence

parts.note: to punt is to gamble, place a bet
Able-Bodied seaman
a locker is a lockable cupboard

explanation.surface: A sailor has stashed medicine in a cupboard aboard a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests a boat, but here it means a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: This class of drug, used for blood pressure and anxiety, is a prescribed medication.

clue.text: Bound to make mistake if inwardly quaking

indicators.note: inwardly means on the inside, so the pieces go within the outer word

parts.note: bound means tied up
to err is to make a mistake
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to slip up if shaking inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', but it is tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shaking with fear is utterly frightened.

clue.text: A frantic call secures top-class mineral

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside, so one word is enclosed

parts.note: the distress signal
best means finest, top-class

explanation.surface: A desperate distress signal gets hold of a first-rate rock.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous silicate is a naturally occurring mineral once used as insulation.

clue.text: Sewed material up to clothe a child

indicators.note: clothing something means wrapping it, so the outer word goes around
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the fabric is reversed

parts.note: denim is a cotton fabric
taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: Someone stitched fabric together to dress a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments machined together have been stitched on a sewing machine.

clue.text: Why the first gag goes wrong?

definitions.text: Why the first gag goes wrong?

indicators.note: something that goes wrong falls out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian's opening joke falls flat, and we ask why.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: nerves explain a fluffed opening line.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervousness before performing is a plausible reason a comic botches the opening joke.

clue.text: Enzyme not originally added to fizzy drink

indicators.note: adding one thing to another joins them end to end

parts.note: Pepsi is a brand of cola

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: No enzyme was put in the soft drink originally.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepsin is the stomach enzyme that breaks down proteins.

clue.text: Property, say, supporting earl

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece comes after

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earl
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A grand property belongs to an earl, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a landed property, often a large country house with grounds.

clue.text: Repeat of "The Choir"

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters belonging to the quoted words, sitting inside them

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A rerun of a television show called The Choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound is a repetition of the original.

clue.text: Publish letter written about army attendant

indicators.note: a letter written about something follows it on the page, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: to air views is to make them public
a host is a great army or multitude
the name of the letter S

explanation.surface: Someone publishes a letter about the army.
explanation.walkthrough: HOST as an army is old biblical usage ('the heavenly host').
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin crew member serving passengers on a plane is a flight attendant.

clue.text: Girl's dismay when losing bishop to knight

indicators.note: one chess piece is lost and another takes its place, so one abbreviation is swapped for the other

parts.note: horror is shock and dismay
Right Reverend, a bishop's title
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A girl is aghast at losing her bishop to a knight in chess.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: the bishop is RR, the Right Reverend, not B.
explanation.definitionFit: Honor is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Abstainer with heart of gold gets tight

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so the metal sits in the centre of the other word

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a non-drinker
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A teetotaller with a heart of gold still gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like drunk, which would be a joke against the abstainer; it means stretched tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled taut is stretched tight with no slack.

clue.text: African verse initially dismissed in regressive article

indicators.note: dismissed at the start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a stanza is a verse of a poem

indicators.note: regressing means going backwards, so the little word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A line of poetry gets thrown out of a backward-looking piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is just the word an.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Tanzania in East Africa is an African.

clue.text: Confused in the main

definitions.meaning: second meaning: out on the ocean, the main being the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly'; in poetic usage the main is the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both bewildered and literally out on the open ocean.

clue.text: Holding back a little, top player's quietened down

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the small amount is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A star tennis player, keeping a little in reserve, has calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedated patient has been calmed with drugs.

clue.text: Squad aboard constantly backing train

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the combination is read in reverse
aboard means on board inside a vessel, so one word goes within another

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
a squad is a military unit

explanation.surface: A squad stays on board a train as it reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the train of followers attending an important person.
